claim: tldraw's maintainer reports a significant increase in contributions generated entirely by AI tools.
quote: Like many other open-source projects on GitHub, we've recently seen a significant increase in contributions generated entirely by AI tools.

claim: According to tldraw, most AI-generated PRs lack context and codebase understanding, and their authors rarely follow up.
quote: most suffer from incomplete or misleading context, misunderstanding of the codebase, and little to no follow-up engagement from their authors

claim: Rust maintainers describe slop contributions as a DDoS on maintenance and moderation capacity.
quote: To put it bluntly, it feels like DDoS against maintenance and moderation capacity.

claim: Astropy maintainers report that even obviously bad AI-generated PRs still cost triage time.
quote: even if these are obviously dead on arrival, they still take time to triage

claim: Some AI-generated PRs look legitimate and reveal their flaws only during in-depth review, so triage alone cannot catch them.
quote: Some of them may look legit at first glance, only revealing flaws when one dive into the code/logic during the review process.

claim: LLVM's policy states that AI tools shift effort from the implementer to the reviewer.
quote: While new tools enable more development, it shifts effort from the implementor to the reviewer

claim: Linux kernel guidelines treat tool-driven contribution volume as a pressure on scarce reviewer bandwidth.
quote: These tools can increase the volume of contributions. At the same time, reviewer and maintainer bandwidth is a scarce resource.

claim: Ghostty frames low-effort AI contributions as pushing the validation burden onto maintainers.
quote: It is rude and disrespectful to approach this boundary with low-effort, unqualified work, since it puts the burden of validation on the maintainer.

claim: scikit-learn will ban users who submit AI-generated content they don't understand, citing maintainer burden.
quote: Due to the burden put on maintainers, users submitting multiple low quality pull requests, or AI generated comments, reviews, issues, or pull requests, where the user does not show a good understanding of what they are posting, might be banned from the organisation.

claim: Zulip's AI policy is motivated by limited maintainer time.
quote: Maintainer time and attention is very limited

claim: QEMU declines contributions believed to contain AI-generated content.
quote: Current QEMU project policy is to DECLINE any contributions which are believed to include or derive from AI generated content.
context: QEMU's stated reason is legal and provenance risk, not review volume, so this is context rather than support.

claim: Godot requires autonomous AI agents to self-disclose and bans agents that don't.
quote: Agents failing to self-disclose will be banned from contributing to the project.
context: Suggests autonomous agents (not just AI-assisted humans) are submitting to large projects.

claim: tldraw closed external PRs because it considered GitHub's existing contribution-management tools inadequate.
quote: This is a temporary policy until GitHub provides better tools for managing contributions.

claim: Ghostty attributes the problem to unqualified contributors, not to AI tools themselves.
quote: It's the people, not the tools, that are the problem.
context: Contradicts framing the problem as 'AI-generated content'. The issue is unreviewed, low-understanding work.

claim: Zulip explicitly permits AI tools, so AI authorship alone isn't treated as the problem.
quote: You can use any tools that help you understand the Zulip codebase and write good code, including AI tools.

claim: curl accepts AI-assisted code, so its concern is quality and verification, not AI use.
quote: We can accept code written with the help of AI into the project

claim: curl reports that fabricated security reports stop real project work.
quote: Fake and otherwise made up security problems effectively prevent us from doing real project work and make us waste time and resources.

claim: curl's contributor guide warns that AI tools frequently produce fabricated findings.
quote: AI-based tools frequently generate inaccurate or fabricated results.

claim: curl no longer offers a bug bounty, saying bounties incentivise made-up problems that cause overload.
quote: A bug bounty gives people too strong incentives to find and make up "problems" in bad faith that cause overload and abuse.

claim: Before LLMs, simply posting a change for review signalled a potential long-term contributor.
quote: posting a change for review was a sign of interest from a potential long-term contributor

claim: The Vouch author argues that the effort of submitting a change no longer filters for trustworthy contributors.
quote: Contributors can no longer be trusted based on the minimal barrier to entry to simply submit a change.

claim: Maintainers used to review every change, a practice that AI-generated volume now strains.
quote: Prior to the advent of LLMs, open source project maintainers would often review any and all changes sent to the project

claim: Across 281 open-source AI contribution policies, 83.3% permit or encourage AI in code contributions.
quote: permission is the norm rather than the exception: 83.3% of policies permit or encourage AI in code contributions
context: Undercuts gating on AI authorship: most projects explicitly allow AI-assisted code.

claim: Most AI policies (67.3%) require a high level of human involvement, which is the property a comprehension gate tries to check.
quote: But permission comes with conditions, as 67.3% require a high level of human involvement and 43.4% assign accountability.

claim: A systematic study found ten distinct countermeasures against AI slop already in use, so the solution space is actively explored.
quote: we identify ten countermeasures against AI slop, targeting pull requests, users, and autonomous agents

claim: An empirical analysis of OSS AI policies finds that protecting scarce maintainer attention is a primary rationale.
quote: these policies seek to protect scarce maintainer attention, preserve accountability, sustain meaningful review interactions, address legal and quality concerns, and maintain pathways for newcomer learning

claim: In 11,097 repositories, AI coding-agent adoption is associated with a 3.7-point drop in newcomers' share of participation.
quote: The relative participation share of newcomers declines significantly by 3.7 percentage points (ATT = -0.037, p < 0.001)
limitations: Measures agent adoption by the repository itself, not inbound AI contributions. Supports the newcomer-pathway concern only indirectly.

claim: The same study finds no significant change in the absolute number of human contributors.
quote: AI agent adoption does not significantly change the absolute number of human contributors (ATT = 0.014, p = 0.224)
context: Tempers claims that AI drives human contributors away. The effect is on relative share.

claim: In 675 security-related agent PRs, rejections often stem from inactivity rather than code content, consistent with engagement being a useful signal.
quote: rejections often arise from social or process factors such as inactivity or missing test coverage
limitations: Different population (agent PRs, security subset). Indirect support for assumption a1.

claim: Flawed AI-generated security contributions are often merged, so review isn't catching all problems.
quote: Many flawed contributions are still merged

claim: In one dataset, reviewers expressed more neutral or positive sentiment toward AI-generated PRs than human ones.
quote: reviewers tend to express more neutral or positive emotions towards AI-generated contributions than human ones
context: Reviewer sentiment in agent-PR datasets doesn't match the frustration expressed in maintainer policies. The populations likely differ (owner-initiated agent PRs vs. unsolicited contributions).

claim: Most AI-generated PRs in the AIDev dataset receive no review at all.
quote: most AI-generated PRs receive no review and, when reviewed, are largely dominated by AI agents rather than humans
context: Suggests much agent PR volume never reaches maintainers' review queues, so the burden is concentrated in specific popular projects.
